sentences.text: This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical) Mode.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

3. Even though this application has been filed seeking grant of regular bail by keeping the sentence under suspension, but in course of hearing, learned counsel for the appellant contended that this application be treated as an application for interim bail for a period of 4 (four) months.

4. It is contended that appellant has been convicted for the offence under Section 376(D) of the IPC and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years and to pay a fine of Rs.50,000/- and in default R.I. for one year.
4.1. It is contended that appellant is in custody all through since 06.09.2013 and he has never availed the // 2 // benefit of Bail/Interim Bail at any point of time.

It is contended that since appellant has already undergone more than half of the sentence and he is in custody since 06.09.2013, appellant be released on interim bail for a period of 4 (four) months on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by keeping the sentence under suspension.
Standing Counsel on the other hand though objected the prayer for grant of interim bail but contended that if this Court is inclined to allow the same, stringent conditions be imposed.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, considering the submissions made and the fact that appellant has already undergone more than half of the sentence, this Court while disposing the I.A.,
Dinabandhu Lohar vs State Of Odisha on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5021140/
1 directs for release of the appellant on interim bail for a period of 4(four) months by keeping the sentence under suspension on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by the learned Court in seisin.
